1.fix: A separate checker keeps only claims backed by a quoted sentence from a page it opened.
1.first: Turn on citations and a link check, then hand-check 20 claims.
1.evl: A link check cut dead or invented links to under 1%

quick.fix: Name one checker per team who opens every cited link and confirms the page holds the sentence.
quick.effort: 2 hours to set up, then about 2 hours a week per checker
quick.limit: It samples claims and misses wrong claims that carry no citation.
quick.when: Hand checks pass about 50 claims a week, or more than 1 in 20 fail

2.fix: Log every failed search, blocked page and cut text, show it above the answer, and never deliver a report with no opened source.
2.first: Ask for the searches run, pages opened and what failed. Reject reports with no sources.

quick.fix: Reject reports with no opened sources and flag every API response carrying a search error code.
quick.effort: 4 hours to add the flag and the rejection rule
quick.limit: A search that finds nothing returns an empty list, not an error.
quick.when: Flagged errors pass about 20 a week

3.fix: Split the question into parts and stop only when each part has evidence or a plain "not found".
3.first: Ask for the plan first, plus a list of what was looked for and not found.
3.evl: Forcing full coverage lifted accuracy 2.7 to 8.2 points in a lab test

quick.fix: Use deep research and edit the shown plan so every sub-question is listed before it starts.
quick.effort: 1 hour to brief the team, then 5 to 10 minutes per question
quick.limit: The tool can still stop early on one sub-question and reports no misses.
quick.when: Research moves to an API workflow, or more than 10 reports a week

4.fix: Use a list of trusted primary sites for high-stakes work, and label every source.
4.first: Write a 20 to 50 site list for one workflow.

quick.fix: Load a 20 to 50 site allow list in ChatGPT Manage sites, Claude Console or allowed_domains.
quick.effort: 4 to 8 hours to build and load one list
quick.limit: A planted page on an allowed site still gets through.
quick.when: A second workflow needs its own list, or lists need monthly review

5.fix: Put today's date in the request, fetch fresh pages, and tell the model when old evidence stopped applying.
5.first: Add "as of today" and source dates to price, rule and people questions.
5.evl: Larger models switched almost perfectly when told evidence had expired

quick.fix: Add an organization instruction to state today's date and the source date beside every changing fact.
quick.limit: page_age is the site update date, and an instruction may not always be followed.
quick.when: An audit sample still finds undated figures in client work

6.fix: Cite only pages that were opened, and report any text that was cut.
6.first: Log whether each cited page was opened, and block those that were not.
6.evl: Opened pages were stale 1.3% of the time, snippets 6.4%

quick.fix: Keep only citations whose URL shows an open_page action, or fetch with citations turned on.
quick.limit: Chat products give no such switch.
quick.when: More than one workflow needs the opened-page rule

7.fix: Name each blocked page, then route to your own copy, a licensed source, a file reader or a browser tool.
7.first: Test whether each team's top 10 sources open, and set a route for the rest.
7.mat: Error codes sold, paid access early
7.evl: Not measured beyond one case of our own

quick.fix: Run the team's top 10 sources through the tool, note failures, and route those to file upload.
quick.limit: A one-time test, and it does not solve unlicensed paywalled sources.
quick.when: Fetch errors need weekly counting by source

8.fix: List the question's assumptions and check each one before searching.
8.first: Add "list and check my assumptions first" to research prompts.
8.evl: A plain prompt gave the same gain as the full check

quick.fix: Add an organization instruction to list a question's assumptions and mark any it could not confirm.
quick.limit: A premise-check instruction can make the model dispute sound premises too.
quick.when: False flags waste more reviewer time than the premises they catch

9.fix: Require a dated primary source for changing facts, with an expiry date.
9.first: Require a dated primary source for prices, rules and office holders.

quick.fix: Force a search on every API call with tool_choice required, and instruct Claude to cite a dated source.
quick.limit: Forcing a search does not stop the model trusting a wrong page.
quick.when: Changing facts appear in more than one client deliverable a week

10.fix: Keep page text away from any model that can act, and ask before actions that follow web content.
10.first: Remove email, payment and file access from browsing agents, and turn on approvals.
10.evl: Attacks got through 12.8% of the time, against 73.1% without

quick.fix: Turn off or allowlist Claude in Chrome, and put staff with email or payment access in Lockdown Mode.
quick.limit: Read-only search can still be steered, and one permissive ChatGPT role restores access.
quick.when: Any browsing agent needs to act on email, payments or files

1.first: Name one person per team who opens every cited source and figure before AI work leaves the company.
1.evl: Grounded legal tools were wrong less often. The human check is not measured

quick.fix: Name one checker per team who opens every cited source and figure and logs each check.
quick.effort: 2 hours to set up, then about 10 minutes per document
quick.limit: Errors in claims that carry no citation, and checker fatigue at volume.
quick.when: The sheet shows more documents than checkers can open in a week

2.first: Turn sandboxes on by policy and give each agent its own low-privilege login.
2.mat: Generally available, often off by default

quick.fix: Block the skip-all-approvals mode in Claude Code's managed settings, and keep the Codex workspace-write sandbox.
quick.limit: Agents' own false reports of success, and agents outside these two tools.
quick.when: More than one agent tool is in use, or agents run unattended

3.first: Pick one approved AI tool with no-training terms and turn on data-loss controls.
3.mat: Generally available, some parts in preview
3.evl: Vendor survey, not cause and effect

quick.fix: Name one licensed enterprise tool for company data, confirm its no-training default, and turn on Purview DLP for Copilot.
quick.limit: Staff who paste into personal accounts, and files uploaded straight into a Copilot prompt.
quick.when: A second AI tool is requested, or a leak is found outside the named tool

4.first: Allow only listed tool servers, and close agents' network access by default.
4.evl: Vendor's own test. Adaptive attacks beat most filters

quick.fix: Set allowedMcpServers with allowManagedMcpServersOnly true in Claude Code, and review the Copilot MCP policy.
quick.limit: Hidden instructions inside approved servers or in pages and files the agent reads.
quick.when: The approved list passes about ten servers, or a second agent tool needs it

5.first: Write the value measure, cost measure and stop rule before the next pilot starts.
5.evl: Analyst survey, a link not proof

quick.fix: Before the next pilot, write one page naming a cost owner, value measure, cost measure and stop date.
quick.limit: Benefits that are hard to price, and pilots already running with no baseline.
quick.when: More than three pilots run at once, or a renewal needs the numbers

6.first: Pin the model version in every production use and keep a list of retirement dates.
6.evl: Model updates broke 24.7% to 47.2% of right answers in a lab test

quick.fix: Pin the exact model ID, set Azure deployments to NoAutoUpgrade, and list each retirement date.
quick.limit: Chat apps where users cannot pin a model, and behaviour changes inside a pinned snapshot.
quick.when: A pinned model is within 90 days of retirement

7.first: Set hard spend caps per person, team and agent.

quick.fix: Set a hard monthly spend limit per OpenAI project and per user limits in Claude Enterprise.
quick.limit: Seat plans with fixed allowances that run out early, and cost per task.
quick.when: Spend spans more than two vendors, or limits are hit monthly

8.first: Test your chatbot with anti-agreement instructions, and route crisis talk to people.
8.evl: Cut agreement with delusions by 73.8% in simulated chats

quick.fix: Add a shared custom instruction to say plainly when it disagrees, then spot-check ten answers a week.
quick.limit: Crisis conversations, which need a human route, and a model that ignores the instruction.
quick.when: The bot faces customers or vulnerable users

9.first: List every agent in one register and rehearse switching one off.

quick.fix: Export the Microsoft 365 Agent Registry into a register with an owner per agent, then rehearse Block.
quick.limit: Agents built outside Microsoft 365, such as coding agents, scripts and other vendors.
quick.when: Agents exist on more than one platform

10.first: Track changes per reviewer and cap incoming AI-written changes.
10.mat: Tools sold, role design in research

quick.fix: Restrict pull request creation to collaborators on busy repos, and track reviews per reviewer weekly.
quick.limit: Internal AI-written changes from staff, who are collaborators already.
quick.when: Reviews per person rise for two months in a row

11.first: Put hard rules in tool settings, not in the prompt.
11.evl: A recap won back about half of a 34-point drop in a lab test

quick.fix: Move the three must-not rules from CLAUDE.md into Claude Code deny rules or a PreToolUse hook.
quick.limit: Lost decisions and facts in long chats, which are not rules.
quick.when: The same rules are needed across several agent tools

12.first: Route AI calls through a gateway with a tested fallback to a second provider.

quick.fix: Subscribe the on-call channel to vendor status pages and switch Bedrock to a cross-Region inference profile.
quick.limit: A full outage at one vendor, since there is no second provider.
quick.when: After the first outage that stops a business process

13.first: Test models on your own harmless but sensitive prompts before choosing filter levels.

quick.fix: Run 20 harmless but sensitive prompts before release and adjust Gemini safety settings only where needed.
quick.limit: Filters you cannot set, such as those in chat apps, and harmful requests that still pass.
quick.when: More than one model or filter is in use

14.first: At the next renewal, add export, notice and no-silent-renewal terms.

quick.fix: At renewal, send a contract letter asking for portability, knowledge transfer, clear licence terms and price transparency.
quick.limit: Prompts tuned to one model, which no contract can move.
quick.when: The first renewal that the letter reaches
